venue.title: Venue | Anthony & Lloyd
venue.para-history-1: Built in 1938, the Temple of Peace is a memorial to those who died in the First World War and home to the <bookLink>Welsh Book of Remembrance</bookLink>, which contains the names of over 35,000 people who died in the conflict.
venue.para-history-2: Once open, it became the headquarters of two significant Welsh organisations. In the Health Wing, the <wnmaLink>Welsh National Memorial Association</wnmaLink> helped eradicate tuberculosis in Wales. In the Peace Wing, the <wlnuLink>Welsh League of Nations Union</wlnuLink> supported the Welsh in campaigning for international cooperation and peace.
venue.para-history-3: Its founder, <daviesLink>Lord David Davies of Llandinam</daviesLink>, hoped it would become a place of pilgrimage to everyone in search of justice, health and peace.
venue.trains-intro: Download the <tfwAppLink>Transport for Wales (TfW) App</tfwAppLink> or use the <tfwJourneyPlannerLink>TfW website</tfwJourneyPlannerLink> to plan your journey, buy tickets and check train times.
venue.buses-intro: There are several bus stops near the venue. The closest is <stopLink>College Road RK on North Road</stopLink>. Download the <appLink>Cardiff Bus app</appLink> or use the <websiteLink>Cardiff Bus website</websiteLink> to plan your journey, buy tickets and check bus times.
